item.title: Personalised GPT News — 16 August 2026
item.description:
The strongest fresh changes are unusually practical: satellite mobile data now works in New Zealand dead zones, Thailand has approved a shorter visa-free stay for New Zealanders, NZ biometric rules have completed their transition, and several new travel, device, privacy and digital-service options are now concrete.

  1. One NZ satellite coverage now carries selected app data as well as messaging. One NZ’s current satellite service can send texts and attachments and provide data for selected apps including WhatsApp and Google Maps in the roughly 40% of New Zealand without terrestrial cell-tower coverage, using compatible phones and plans. That materially changes what a normal phone can do on remote drives and outdoor trips without a separate satellite device. Source — One NZ, updated 23 Jul 2026.
  2. (Travel) Thailand has approved cutting New Zealanders’ visa-free stay from 60 days to 30 days. Thailand’s Cabinet approved withdrawal of the 60-day exemption and a revised 30-day visa-free scheme; New Zealand remains in the 30-day group. The revised regime is not yet in force: it takes effect 15 days after the relevant Ministry of Interior notices are published in the Royal Gazette, so the existing 60-day entitlement remains until then. Source — Royal Thai Government PRD, 15 Jul 2026.
  3. (Privacy) New Zealand’s biometric privacy transition period ended on 3 August. Organisations and businesses that were already using facial recognition, fingerprints, voice patterns, gait, keystroke patterns or other biometric processing have now reached the end of the nine-month transition period for the Biometric Processing Privacy Code 2025. The Code sets specific collection, use, disclosure, retention and security rules under the Privacy Act. Source — Office of the Privacy Commissioner, transition ended 3 Aug 2026.
  4. Google unveiled the Pixel 11 generation and a new Android item tracker. Google announced the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL and 11 Pro Fold, all using Tensor G6, plus Pixel Watch 5 and the new UWB-enabled Pixel Tag. Phone and watch pre-orders opened 12 August with general sales from 20 August; Pixel Tag is scheduled for November. Source — WIRED, 12 Aug 2026.
  5. EU AI transparency rules are now in force and are changing global AI outputs. From 2 August, Article 50 of the EU AI Act requires specified AI systems to disclose AI interaction and imposes marking requirements for generated or manipulated content, with a transition until 2 December for some pre-existing systems. Anthropic has separately announced machine-readable provenance/watermarking for Claude-generated text and images across its platforms globally. Source — European Commission, rules applicable 2 Aug 2026; Source — The Verge, 12 Aug 2026.
  6. (Australia) Auckland will gain a direct Western Sydney International service when the new airport opens. From 26 October, Air New Zealand plans three Auckland–Western Sydney return services each week, making it the new airport’s first international airline and giving New Zealand travellers a second Sydney airport option. Source — Air New Zealand, 17 Jul 2026.
  7. New Zealand’s all-of-government app now includes a working digital-wallet shell. The second release of the Govt.nz app lets users set up its accredited-credential wallet now, alongside pinned government services and location-based emergency updates. The first usable accredited credentials are expected to begin arriving progressively from late August; the app itself does not require an account and stores preferences on the device. Source — New Zealand Government, current release.
  8. Samsung’s 2026 foldables reached general availability. Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8 and Z Flip8 entered general availability on 7 August after their July launch. The Fold8 Ultra adds Samsung’s largest foldable display and 200MP camera system, while the Fold8 and Flip8 refresh the two mainstream form factors. Source — Samsung, availability 7 Aug 2026.
  9. (Longevity) Human muscle data linked long-term training with markedly fewer age-related molecular differences. A Nature Aging multi-omics study found that trained older adults lacked about 50% of the age-related skeletal-muscle molecular differences seen when older and young adults of comparable activity were contrasted, while preserving expression of key cellular-respiration and energy-metabolism genes and showing stronger acute exercise responses with greater fitness. Source — Nature Aging, 3 Jul 2026.
  10. (Melbourne Fabric) Multiple Melbourne employers are simultaneously recruiting for substantial Microsoft Fabric build, lead and support work. Current openings include a senior Power BI/Fabric developer role described as driving Fabric adoption, a Data Engineering Lead for a financial-services organisation’s modern Fabric platform, and two BAU Fabric support-engineer positions for a lakehouse/pipelines/Power BI platform. Taken together, these are concrete concurrent enterprise-demand signals rather than a single generic advert. Source — Konnexus role; Source — SustainRecruit role; Source — Logical roles, Aug 2026.
  11. (NZ Tenancy) New methamphetamine tenancy thresholds are now legally operative. Since 16 April, a rental is classed as meth-contaminated where tested areas exceed 15 micrograms per 100 cm² and must be decontaminated to that level or below; areas above 30 micrograms per 100 cm² make a property uninhabitable and can trigger much shorter tenancy-termination notices depending on circumstances. Source — Tenancy Services, effective 16 Apr 2026.
  12. EU countries adopted the first major overhaul of air-passenger rights in more than 20 years. The July revision adds free adjacent seating for children under 12 with an accompanying adult, clearer baggage-fee information, simpler reimbursement/compensation procedures, stronger rerouting and connecting-journey protections, and stronger protection for disabled travellers and mobility equipment. The new rules are expected to enter into force next summer and will apply to covered flights used by visitors as well as EU residents. Source — European Commission, 28 Jul 2026.
  13. (Gaming) Two modern Star Ocean games are now sold DRM-free. Star Ocean The Divine Force and Star Ocean The Second Story R joined GOG on 28 July, giving buyers downloadable DRM-free versions rather than requiring the Steam release; GOG also said it is working on stronger Linux support. Source — GOG, 28 Jul 2026.
  14. Christchurch is getting an additional nonstop Singapore service from Air New Zealand. Air New Zealand will add three weekly Christchurch–Singapore Boeing 787 services for the 25 October 2026–27 March 2027 northern-winter season. Together with Singapore Airlines’ existing service, the partners plan up to 15 weekly Christchurch–Singapore flights in peak months. Source — Air New Zealand, 28 May 2026.
  15. Auckland is regaining nonstop Papua New Guinea flights after 26 years. Air Niugini plans three weekly Auckland–Port Moresby services from 17 November, timed with onward connections to Manila, Tokyo, Hong Kong and Singapore. The route creates a new direct adventure destination and another Asia-connection path from New Zealand. Source — Auckland Airport, 17 Jul 2026.
  16. (Wellington) Te Papa is opening a major seven-century Māori carving exhibition. He Toi Whakairo — The Art of Māori Carving opens 29 August with 147 carvings spanning seven centuries, including works that have not previously been exhibited. This is a genuinely new Wellington activity rather than a recurring event listing. Source — Te Papa, opening 29 Aug 2026.
  17. (Crypto & finances) Kiwibank has entered New Zealand’s regulated open-banking payments regime. Kiwibank became a designated data holder for payment services from 1 June 2026 under the Customer and Product Data framework, joining ANZ, ASB, BNZ and Westpac in regulated open banking; Kiwibank’s broader account-information obligation follows in December. This expands the set of bank customers whose authorised payment functionality can be exposed through regulated open-banking services. Source — MBIE, 2026 implementation timeline.
  18. (Entertainment) Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now in cinemas. Sony’s new Tom Holland Spider-Man film opened theatrically on 31 July, making it the single entertainment release selected for this briefing under the one-item cap. Source — Sony Pictures, 31 Jul 2026.

item.title: Personalised GPT News — 16 August 2026
item.description:
Fresh developments include new cancer and Alzheimer’s approvals, concrete Australian digital-policy changes, a new federally supervised crypto bank, and several consumer-facing technology and payment shifts.

  1. FDA approves a new oral multiple-myeloma treatment. On 13 August, the US FDA approved Bristol Myers Squibb’s Zenbexus (iberdomide) with Darzalex and dexamethasone for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. The accelerated approval is based on late-stage data and requires confirmatory clinical benefit. Source — Reuters, 13 Aug 2026.
  2. FDA approves a new tau PET imaging agent for Alzheimer’s assessment. On 14 August, Lantheus said the FDA approved Tauklarify, a radioactive PET imaging agent that makes abnormal tau deposits visible in cognitively impaired adults being assessed for Alzheimer’s disease. Source — Reuters, 14 Aug 2026.
  3. (Crypto & finances) World Liberty Financial receives conditional US national trust-bank approval. On 14 August, the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency conditionally approved a national trust-bank charter for World Liberty Financial, allowing the firm to expand federally supervised stablecoin and custody activities subject to stated conditions. Source — Reuters, 14 Aug 2026.
  4. (Australia) Australia introduces revised legislation requiring large digital platforms to strike more local-news payment deals. On 12 August, Australia introduced a revised media-licensing bill requiring covered platforms to strike deals with at least eight local media companies, with a levy liability equal to 2.5% of Australian advertising revenue and 5% of collected funds allocated to Australian Associated Press. Source — Reuters, 12 Aug 2026.
  5. (Travel) The US made its visa-bond programme permanent for applicants from 50 countries. In August, the US State Department made permanent a programme allowing consular officers to require refundable tourist or business visa bonds of up to US$20,000 from applicants in designated countries; the current list covers 50 countries and can be expanded with notice. Source — Reuters, 12 Aug 2026.
  6. (Privacy) Australia’s Origin Energy disclosed a potential customer-data security incident. On 22 July, Origin Energy said it was investigating possible unauthorised access to some customer data. It said it did not expect affected data to include customer credit-card or bank details and notified Australian cyber, police and privacy authorities. Source — Reuters via Yahoo, 22 Jul 2026.
  7. (Australia) Australia announced a central government Office of AI and planned data-centre resource rules. On 14 July, Australia announced an Office of AI within the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet. The government also said planned legislation would set rules for large data centres, including limits on water use and a requirement to be net producers of energy. Source — Reuters, 14 Jul 2026.
  8. FDA approves Replimune’s tumour-injected melanoma therapy after earlier rejections. On 6 August, the FDA approved Tudriqev (RP1) with Opdivo for advanced melanoma after prior treatment failure. RP1 is a genetically modified herpes virus injected directly into tumours; confirmatory Phase III work remains under way. Source — Reuters, 6 Aug 2026.
  9. Merck’s first-in-class oral PCSK9 cholesterol drug was approved. On 16 July, the FDA approved Merck’s Lipfendra (enlicitide), the first oral treatment in the PCSK9-inhibitor class. Trials reported LDL reductions of nearly 60% with once-daily dosing. Source — Reuters, 16 Jul 2026.
  10. Lilly reported additional Phase III retatrutide obesity results and set a Q1 2027 FDA filing target. On 23 July, Lilly reported two more late-stage trials of retatrutide. In an 80-week study of adults with severe obesity and heart disease, the highest dose produced average weight loss of 22.6%; in another trial involving obesity and type 2 diabetes, average weight loss reached 20.8%. Source — Reuters, 23 Jul 2026.
  11. A registrational rectal-cancer study reported sustained complete clinical responses with dostarlimab. On 13 July, GSK said the Phase II AZUR-1 trial of Jemperli (dostarlimab) in dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer met its primary objective, with a clinically meaningful rate of participants showing no detectable cancer at 12 months or longer after treatment. Source — GSK regulatory announcement via Reuters/TradingView, 13 Jul 2026.
  12. FDA approves GSK’s targeted drug for previously treated ROS1-positive lung cancer. On 22 July, GSK announced FDA approval of Jideytro (zidesamtinib) for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer previously treated with a ROS1 kinase inhibitor. Source — GSK regulatory announcement via Reuters/TradingView, 22 Jul 2026.
  13. FDA approves a wearable injector version of Sanofi’s Sarclisa. On 10 July, the FDA approved Sarclisa Escena, allowing the multiple-myeloma drug to be delivered under the skin through an on-body wearable injector rather than only by intravenous infusion. Source — Reuters via Investing.com, 10 Jul 2026.
  14. Biogen’s anti-tau Alzheimer’s drug reduced tau substantially in a mid-stage trial, despite missing its dose-response primary endpoint. On 14 July, researchers reported that diranersen reduced tau by roughly 50% to 65% across studied doses. The lowest dose also showed slower cognitive decline on five of six assessment tools; Biogen plans a pivotal Phase III trial in 2027. Source — Reuters, 14 Jul 2026.
  15. Google was ordered to open Android functions and some anonymised search-optimisation data to qualifying rivals in the EU. On 16 July, the European Commission specified Digital Markets Act measures requiring Google to open 11 Android functions to rival AI assistants from July 2027 and to share qualifying anonymised search-optimisation data with competing search/AI services from January 2027, subject to security and privacy checks. Source — Reuters, 16 Jul 2026.
  16. (Privacy) EU lawmakers backed temporary child-abuse detection rules while exempting end-to-end encrypted communications. On 9 July, EU lawmakers backed reinstating temporary online child-sexual-abuse detection rules but voted to exempt end-to-end encrypted communications such as WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal from the interim scanning regime. Source — Reuters via Investing.com, 9 Jul 2026.
  17. (Privacy) EU regulators told Meta to change addictive Facebook and Instagram design features or risk fines. On 10 July, the European Commission issued preliminary findings that Meta had not adequately addressed risks linked to highly personalised recommendations, autoplay and infinite scroll under the Digital Services Act, and demanded changes or the company could face penalties. Source — Reuters via MarketScreener, 10 Jul 2026.
  18. ChatGPT Work and GPT-5.6 launched publicly. On 9 July, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, combining ChatGPT with Codex-style agentic capabilities for producing documents, presentations, websites and other multi-step work, alongside the GPT-5.6 model family. Source — Reuters via Investing.com, 9 Jul 2026.
  19. The ECB selected 36 payment providers for the digital-euro pilot. On 14 July, the European Central Bank selected 36 banks and payment providers, including Deutsche Bank, UniCredit and Revolut, for a 12-month pilot scheduled to begin in the second half of 2027. The beta transactions will test technical and user-interface functions but will not yet constitute legal tender. Source — Reuters, 14 Jul 2026.
  20. Samsung launched its first US co-branded credit card, fully integrated with Samsung Wallet. On 20 July, Samsung and Barclays launched the Galaxy Card on Visa’s network. Users can apply, manage the account, track spending and redeem rewards through Samsung Wallet, with 5% cash back on Samsung purchases. Source — Reuters, 20 Jul 2026.
